description: Full-stack synchronous collaboration layer: real-time 1-on-1 and group text chat, WebRTC video/audio calls, one-to-many live sessions, presence system, calendar with external sync, meeting scheduling, collaborative agendas, screen sharing, recording, AI transcription, auto-summarisation, and meeting minutes with task assignment.

architectureNotes.realtimeTransport: Socket.IO on the Express back-end (back/) for all real-time events (chat, presence, signalling). Namespaces: /chat, /presence, /signalling, /live.
architectureNotes.videoInfrastructure: Self-hosted LiveKit server (Docker) for WebRTC media routing. Front-end uses livekit-client SDK. Back-end issues short-lived access tokens via LiveKit Server SDK.
architectureNotes.aiPipeline: OpenAI Whisper API for speech-to-text transcription of recordings. OpenAI GPT-4o (or Anthropic claude-3-5-sonnet) for summarisation and meeting-minutes generation. Provider abstracted behind a back/src/services/ai-provider.ts interface so it can be swapped.
architectureNotes.calendarSync: Google Calendar API (OAuth 2.0) and Microsoft Graph API (OAuth 2.0 / MSAL) for external calendar read/write. In-app calendar is the source of truth; external events are mirrored via webhooks.
architectureNotes.storage: Recordings stored to S3-compatible object storage (MinIO in dev, AWS S3 in prod). Transcripts and summaries stored in PostgreSQL.

presence-001.title: User Presence & Availability System
presence-001.description: Real-time presence tracking: online/away/busy/do-not-disturb/offline statuses with user-set custom status messages and automatic idle detection. Presence state is broadcast over Socket.IO /presence namespace and stored in Redis for fast fan-out.
presence-001.implementation: Create presence context at src/contexts/PresenceContext.tsx. Connect to Socket.IO /presence namespace on auth. Emit heartbeat every 30 s; server marks user away after 5 min of silence, offline after 15 min. Status stored in Redis hash presence:{userId}. Expose usePresence(userId) hook that subscribes to presence:{userId} events. Show coloured dot badge on avatars throughout the app.
backendWork: back/src/sockets/presence.socket.ts — namespace /presence with events: join, heartbeat, set-status, disconnect
back/src/services/presence.service.ts — Redis get/set with TTL, fan-out to connected clients in same org
back/src/routes/presence.route.ts — REST GET /api/presence/batch for bulk status fetch on page load
acceptanceCriteria: User status dot appears on all avatars across sidebar, chat lists, and member directories
Status updates propagate to all online org members within 1 s
User can manually set status from navbar avatar dropdown
Idle detection sets status to away after 5 min without input
Custom status message (max 100 chars) shown in tooltips
Redis TTL prevents stale presence entries surviving server restart
Status persists across page navigations (socket reconnects)
Presence badge visible in 1-on-1 and group chat headers

chat-002.title: Real-Time 1-on-1 Text Chat
chat-002.description: Full-featured direct messaging between two users. Messages delivered in real-time via Socket.IO, persisted to PostgreSQL, and rendered in a threaded scrollable panel. Supports text, emoji reactions, @mentions, file attachments, read receipts, and typing indicators.
chat-002.implementation: Expand existing chat sidebar (chat-001) into a full chat module. Route: /chat/dm/[userId]. Create chat repository at src/lib/repositories/chat.repository.ts. Backend socket namespace /chat with rooms dm:{smallerId}:{largerId}. Messages stored in messages table (id, roomId, senderId, content, type, parentId, createdAt). Optimistic UI updates with server confirmation rollback.
backendWork: back/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts — /chat namespace; events: join-room, send-message, typing, read-receipt, add-reaction, delete-message
features: Typing indicators with debounce (stop after 3 s)
Read receipts (single tick = sent, double tick = read)
File & image attachments (up to 25 MB, stored S3)
acceptanceCriteria: Messages appear on recipient screen within 500 ms on local network
History loads via pagination (50 messages per page)
Typing indicator appears within 1 s and disappears 3 s after user stops
Read receipts update correctly for both participants
File attachments upload with progress bar and can be downloaded
Emoji reactions toggle on click; count displayed
Edited messages show (edited) label
Deleted messages show 'Message deleted' placeholder
Thread replies open in side panel without navigating away
All interactions work in both light and dark theme
All strings use t() for i18n

chat-003.title: Real-Time Group Text Chat
chat-003.description: Multi-user group channels scoped to teams or projects. Supports all 1-on-1 chat features plus channel management: create/rename/archive channels, add/remove members, pin messages, and channel-level notification preferences.
chat-003.implementation: Route: /chat/channel/[channelId]. Room ID is channel:{channelId}. Channel entity stored in channels table (id, name, teamId | projectId, createdBy, isArchived). Membership in channel_members table. Pin state in pinned_messages table. Sidebar shows channel list grouped by workspace (team/project), sorted by most recent activity.
backendWork: back/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts — extend /chat with group events: join-channel, leave-channel, pin-message, update-channel
back/src/routes/channel.route.ts — CRUD for channels and membership
acceptanceCriteria: Channel list in left sidebar updates in real time when new messages arrive (bold name, unread count badge)
@ mentions notify the mentioned user even if not in the channel view
Pinned messages panel accessible from channel header
Only channel admins can rename, archive, or delete
Notification preferences (all messages / mentions only / mute) persist per user per channel
Archived channels hidden from sidebar but searchable
Channel member list shows presence dots

video-001.title: LiveKit Infrastructure & Token Service
video-001.description: Self-hosted LiveKit SFU provisioned via Docker Compose alongside the existing PostgreSQL container. Express back-end exposes a token-generation endpoint. This is the infrastructure task that all video/audio features depend on.
video-001.implementation: Add livekit service to docker-compose.yml. Create back/src/services/livekit.service.ts wrapping livekit-server-sdk. Expose POST /api/livekit/token {roomName, participantIdentity, participantName, permissions}. Tokens are JWT-signed with LIVEKIT_API_KEY + LIVEKIT_API_SECRET env vars. Room names follow convention: dm:{roomId}, call:{callId}, live:{sessionId}.
backendWork: docker-compose.yml — add livekit service (livekit/livekit-server), port 7880 (HTTPS) and 7881 (TCP/UDP media)
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose up starts LiveKit alongside PostgreSQL
POST /api/livekit/token returns valid JWT token within 200 ms
Token grants correct permissions (publish, subscribe, room join)
Tokens expire after 4 h
Unauthenticated requests to token endpoint return 401

video-002.title: 1-on-1 Video & Audio Call
video-002.description: Peer-to-peer-quality video and audio calls between two users, routed through LiveKit SFU. Initiated from DM chat header or contact cards. Includes camera on/off, mic mute, screen share, call timer, and end-call.
video-002.implementation: Inbound call triggers a Socket.IO call-invite event. Recipient sees a floating call-notification overlay. On accept both sides fetch a LiveKit token for the same room and connect via @livekit/components-react <LiveKitRoom>. Render using VideoConference preset component, customised with our design tokens. Route: /call/[callId] (opens in a new browser tab or modal overlay, configurable).
backendWork: back/src/sockets/call.socket.ts — /signalling namespace; events: call-invite, call-accept, call-reject, call-end, call-busy
features: Missed call notification stored in notifications table
acceptanceCriteria: Call invite notification appears on recipient's screen within 1 s
Recipient can accept or reject; caller sees state change within 1 s
Video and audio streams connect within 3 s of both parties joining on local network
Camera and mic controls work without page reload
Ending the call disconnects both parties and records call duration in DB
Missed calls show in notification bell with timestamp

video-003.title: Screen Sharing
video-003.description: Any participant in a 1-on-1 call, group call, or live session can share their entire screen, a specific window, or a browser tab. Multiple participants may share simultaneously (viewer can switch between screenshares).
video-003.implementation: Use LiveKit's built-in screen share track (participant.screenShareTrack). Add Share Screen button to call-controls.tsx. Share source picker is the browser native getDisplayMedia() dialog. Screenshare tile appears in a dedicated panel above the speaker tile. Annotation layer is out of scope for v3.
acceptanceCriteria: Share Screen button visible in call controls
Browser picker shown to select source
Screenshare tile displayed prominently for all participants
Participant can stop sharing at any time
Multiple simultaneous shares supported; viewers switch via tab strip

video-004.title: Group Video & Audio Call
video-004.description: Video/audio calls for 3–50 participants within a channel or team. Grid layout auto-adjusts from 2×2 to 5×5. Active speaker detection highlights the dominant speaker. All features of 1-on-1 calls plus hand-raise and reactions.
video-004.implementation: Extend call-room.tsx to support multi-participant grid. Use LiveKit's useParticipants() hook. Implement active-speaker detection via useSpeakingParticipants(). Layout switches: grid (≤9 participants), speaker-focus (>9, dominant speaker large, others strip). Group calls initiated from channel header 'Start Call' button. All channel members receive invite via Socket.IO.
features: Hand raise (shows animated hand icon on tile)
Quick emoji reactions (thumbs-up, heart, laugh, clap — float and fade)
acceptanceCriteria: Up to 50 participants can join the same LiveKit room
Grid layout renders correctly for 2, 4, 9, and 25 participants
Active speaker switch latency < 500 ms
Hand raise icon visible to all participants within 1 s
Emoji reactions float and fade after 3 s
Host can remove a participant; removed participant sees call-ended screen
All controls (mute, camera, share, hand, react, end) visible on mobile

video-005.title: One-to-Many Live Video Session (Webinar / Broadcast)
video-005.description: A host (or co-hosts) broadcasts video/audio to up to 500 viewers. Viewers are receive-only by default but can be promoted to speaker. Includes live Q&A, polls, viewer count, and hand-raise queue for the host.
video-005.implementation: LiveKit room with host publishing tracks and viewers joining with subscribe-only permissions. Token endpoint differentiates role via canPublish flag. Route: /live/[sessionId]. Session entity in live_sessions table. Sidebar shows Q&A queue and polls panel. Broadcast can be promoted to 'session recording' (video-008).
backendWork: back/src/routes/live-session.route.ts — CRUD for live sessions, POST /api/live-sessions/:id/promote-speaker, POST /api/live-sessions/:id/polls
back/src/sockets/live.socket.ts — /live namespace; events: qa-submit, qa-answer, poll-create, poll-vote, promote-viewer, lower-hand
acceptanceCriteria: Host can start a session and share the viewer link
Up to 500 viewers can join with audio/video muted and receive-only tokens
Viewer count updates in real time
Host can promote a viewer to speaker (viewer's mic/camera unlock)

video-006.title: Call & Session Recording
video-006.description: Hosts can record group calls, meeting calls, and live sessions. Recording is composed server-side by LiveKit's Egress service, uploaded to S3, and made available for playback in the app. Participants see a recording indicator badge.
video-006.implementation: Enable LiveKit Egress in docker-compose.yml (livekit/egress image). When host clicks 'Record', back-end calls egress.startRoomCompositeEgress() with S3 output config. On completion webhook, store S3 URL in recordings table and link to the meeting or session. Front-end uses wavesurfer.js for waveform playback preview.
acceptanceCriteria: Record button visible to host only in call controls
REC badge appears for all participants when recording starts
Recording stops when host clicks Stop or when call ends
Recording available in /recordings page within 2 min of call end
Playback works in-browser with seek, play/pause, volume
Recordings can be downloaded or deleted (host/admin only)
Recording consent prompt shown to participants before host can record

ai-001.title: AI Provider Abstraction & Transcription Service
ai-001.description: Single AI provider service in the back-end that wraps OpenAI (primary) and Anthropic (fallback) SDKs, and exposes a transcription endpoint that accepts audio file references and returns text via OpenAI Whisper.
ai-001.implementation: Create back/src/services/ai-provider.ts with methods: transcribe(s3Key): Promise<string>, summarise(transcript: string, context: MeetingContext): Promise<Summary>, generateMinutes(transcript: string, attendees: User[], agendaItems: AgendaItem[]): Promise<MeetingMinutes>. The transcription job is queued via a Redis queue (BullMQ) to avoid blocking the HTTP request.
acceptanceCriteria: Transcription job queued within 500 ms of recording becoming ready
Transcription status polled via GET endpoint and shown in UI as a progress badge
Transcription completes for a 60-min recording in < 5 min
Transcript stored in PostgreSQL transcripts table linked to recording
Provider can be switched via AI_PROVIDER env var without code change
Failed jobs retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff

ai-002.title: Auto Meeting Summarisation
ai-002.description: After a meeting recording is transcribed, automatically generate a structured summary: key discussion points, decisions made, and open questions. Summary is attached to the meeting record and emailed to attendees.
ai-002.implementation: After ai-001 transcription completes, chain a summarisation job. Pass transcript + meeting metadata (title, attendees, agenda) to GPT-4o with a structured output prompt. Store result in meeting_summaries table as JSON {keyPoints: string[], decisions: string[], openQuestions: string[]}. Trigger email notification to attendees via existing email service.
acceptanceCriteria: Summary auto-generated within 2 min of transcription completing
Summary section visible on meeting detail page
Key points, decisions, and open questions rendered as distinct sections
Attendees receive email with summary within 5 min of meeting end
User can regenerate summary if result is unsatisfactory (host only)

ai-003.title: Automated Meeting Minutes with Task Assignment
ai-003.description: From the meeting transcript and attendee list, generate formal meeting minutes (date, attendees, agenda items, discussion per item, action items) and auto-create tasks in AltiTeam linked to the meeting, pre-assigned to the mentioned team member.
ai-003.implementation: Extend ai-provider.ts generateMinutes() method with a JSON-mode prompt that returns {attendees, agendaDiscussions: [{agendaItem, discussion, outcome}], actionItems: [{description, assigneeName, dueDate}]}. Back-end fuzzy-matches assigneeName against org members. Creates task entities via existing tasks repository. User is shown a confirmation/edit dialog before tasks are committed.
taskCreationFlow: Host/organiser sees review dialog listing proposed tasks
Can edit description, assignee, and due date before confirming
Confirmed tasks created in tasks repository and appear in assignee's My Tasks
Created tasks linked back to meeting via meeting_tasks join table
acceptanceCriteria: Meeting minutes page shows structured document with all sections
Action items extracted from transcript with ≥ 80 % accuracy on test corpus
Assignee fuzzy-match correctly maps names to org members ≥ 90 % of the time
Confirmation dialog lists proposed tasks with edit controls before creating

calendar-001.title: In-App Calendar
calendar-001.description: Full-featured in-app calendar rendered with FullCalendar (React). Views: month, week, day, and agenda list. Events include meetings, tasks with due dates, and live sessions. User can create, edit, and delete events directly from the calendar.
calendar-001.implementation: Install @fullcalendar/react + plugins. Route: /calendar. The calendar queries GET /api/calendar/events?start=&end= which aggregates meetings, tasks, and live sessions into a unified CalendarEvent DTO. Events colour-coded by type. Clicking an event opens a detail sheet. Creating an event opens a new-meeting dialog (calendar-002 flow).
backendWork: back/src/routes/calendar.route.ts — GET /api/calendar/events (aggregates meetings + tasks + live sessions), POST /api/calendar/events
acceptanceCriteria: Calendar renders at /calendar with month/week/day/agenda views
Events from meetings, tasks, and live sessions all appear
Clicking an event shows detail sheet with join/view links
Creating an event from calendar opens pre-filled meeting dialog
Navigating months/weeks fetches events for the visible range only
Mini-calendar widget in sidebar shows dot for days with events
Calendar is responsive (week view on desktop, day view on mobile)

calendar-002.title: Meeting Scheduling with Agenda
calendar-002.description: Full meeting scheduling flow: set title, date/time, duration, recurrence, location/link, invite attendees, and build a structured agenda before the meeting. Invitees receive email invitations and in-app notifications.
calendar-002.implementation: New meeting dialog at src/components/meeting/new-meeting-dialog.tsx. Multi-step form: (1) Basic Info, (2) Attendees, (3) Agenda Builder, (4) Review & Send. Meeting stored in meetings table. Agenda items in agenda_items table (id, meetingId, order, title, duration, presenter, notes). Meeting generates a unique /meetings/[id] URL sent in invites. LiveKit room pre-created on schedule.
backendWork: back/src/services/meeting.service.ts — create, update, delete, send invites via email service
features: Per-item timer visible during meeting (ai-002 integration)
RSVP tracking (accepted/declined/tentative) with email response links
Add video call link automatically (LiveKit room URL)
acceptanceCriteria: Meeting form validates required fields before step progression
Agenda items can be added, removed, and reordered via drag handle
Attendee search finds org members by name or email
Invite emails sent within 60 s of meeting creation

calendar-003.title: Google Calendar & Microsoft Outlook Sync
calendar-003.description: Two-way sync between AltiTeam in-app calendar and external Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook. User connects their account via OAuth. AltiTeam meetings are pushed to the external calendar. External events are pulled and shown (read-only) in the AltiTeam calendar.
calendar-003.implementation: OAuth flow for Google (googleapis) and Microsoft (MSAL + Microsoft Graph API). Store OAuth tokens in calendar_integrations table (userId, provider, accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, calendarId). Push: when a meeting is created/updated/deleted in AltiTeam, call Google Calendar events.insert() or Graph calendarView PATCH. Pull: subscribe to push notifications (Google Calendar push channel, Microsoft Graph subscription webhook) to sync external events on change. Nightly cron job re-syncs as fallback.
syncRules: AltiTeam meetings push to external calendar with video join link in description
External events imported as read-only; shown in grey on in-app calendar
Deleting an AltiTeam meeting also deletes the external event
Rescheduling syncs new time to external calendar
External cancellations set external event as cancelled; in-app event unchanged
acceptanceCriteria: Settings → Integrations page shows Google Calendar and Outlook connection cards
OAuth flow completes without leaving AltiTeam (popup window strategy)
Connected status shown with last-sync timestamp

Rescheduled meeting updates external calendar within 30 s

meeting-room-001.title: Live Meeting Room with Agenda Timer
meeting-room-001.description: When a scheduled meeting starts, participants join a live meeting room page that combines the video call (video-004), the meeting agenda with a per-item countdown timer, and the collaborative meeting doc (meeting-room-002). The organiser controls agenda progression.
meeting-room-001.implementation: Route: /meetings/[meetingId]/room. Full-page layout with three panels: left (video grid, 60 %), center-right (agenda + timer), right (collaborative doc, collapsible). Agenda timer counts down duration for the current item; organiser presses Next Item to advance. Timer reaching zero triggers a soft chime and auto-advances. Meeting status updates to in-progress when first participant joins.
acceptanceCriteria: Joining /meetings/[id]/room before start time shows a lobby countdown

meeting-room-002.title: Collaborative Meeting Document
meeting-room-002.description: A shared real-time text document attached to every meeting, editable by all participants simultaneously during the call. Pre-populated with the meeting agenda as a template. Notes persist after the meeting and are linked from the meeting detail page.
meeting-room-002.implementation: Use a CRDT-based approach: Yjs + y-socket.io on the back-end for real-time collaborative editing. Document stored as Yjs binary state in meeting_documents table (meetingId, ydocState bytea, updatedAt). Front-end renders with TipTap editor (headless, Tailwind-styled) using the @tiptap/extension-collaboration extension. On meeting creation, document is bootstrapped with agenda items as H2 headings.
backendWork: back/src/sockets/ydoc.socket.ts — y-socket.io server binding, room = doc:{meetingId}
features: Real-time collaborative editing (multiple cursors with user colours)

Auto-saves every 10 s and on disconnect

notifications-001.title: Push & Desktop Notifications
notifications-001.description: Browser push notifications (Web Push API) and in-app notification centre for all synchronous events: incoming calls, meeting reminders (15 min, 5 min, at start), new DMs, @mentions, RSVP responses, and live session starts.
notifications-001.implementation: Service Worker (public/sw.js) registers Web Push subscription. Back-end stores subscription in push_subscriptions table. Sends push via web-push library. In-app: NotificationContext polls GET /api/notifications?unread=true on mount and subscribes to Socket.IO notification:{userId} events. Notification bell in navbar shows unread count badge.
backendWork: back/src/workers/meeting-reminder.worker.ts — cron job, fires 15 min and 5 min before meetings
